title: FLInt 2.0 Integration in C. elegans
author: Nawaphat Malaiwong
materials: Culture tdTomato-expressing worms (see ‘Materials’) at 16°C or 20°C to obtain healthy young adults Select well-fed, young adult worms using a paintbrush under a dissecting microscope Transfer worms using halocarbon oil and mount the worms onto 2% agarose pad on coverslip NOTE: For double cutting sites using crRNAs (H2B + unc-119), the tdTomato strain should be outcrossed with N2 to eliminate the unc-119(ed3) allele. The outcrossed strains will be generated and deposited to CGC

steps.title: Prepare FLInt 2.0 RNP complex
steps.instruction: In a 10 µL total volume combine 1 µL of 100 µM crRNA (FLInt2.0*, IDT) to reach 10 µM final crRNA, 0.5 µL of 200 µM tracrRNA (IDT) to reach 10 µM final tracrRNA, 1 µL of 62 µM Cas9 endonuclease (IDT) to reach 6.2 µM final Cas9, and 7.5 µL nuclease‑free water. Adjust crRNA composition for the desired cut strategy (single‑cut: add crRNA(H2B); double‑cut: add crRNA(H2B) + crRNA(unc‑119) and increase tracrRNA to 20 µM; linearized plasmid: add crRNA(ampR) and 20 µM tracrRNA). Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 30 minutes. Aliquot 2 µL of the RNP mix into a PCR tube and store at –20 °C for later use. Note that the RNP volume can be higher than 2 µL for better efficiency.

steps.title: Assemble injection DNA mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the injection mix according to the standard protocol: add plasmid of interest at x ng/µL, co‑injection marker at y ng/µL, and, if needed, 1 kb Plus DNA ladder (Invitrogen) to bring the total DNA concentration to 100 ng/µL. (Optional) add 1 µL of 100 µM ssODN (1) and 1 µL of 100 µM ssODN (2). Add 2 µL of the FLInt2.0 RNP mix (or a higher volume if desired for efficiency). Finally add nuclease‑free water to reach a total volume of 10 µL.

steps.title: Centrifuge injection mixture
steps.instruction: Spin the completed injection mixture at 12,000 rpm for 5–10 minutes before use.

steps.title: Inject mixture into P0 gonads
steps.instruction: Inject the mixture into a single gonad or both gonads of each P0 worm using standard micro‑injection technique (critical for obtaining integrants).

steps.title: Recover injected worms on plates
steps.instruction: Immediately after injection transfer 10–15 injected P0 worms to a 5‑cm NGM plate seeded with OP50 and incubate the plate at 25 °C.

steps.title: Assess early array‑positive F1
steps.instruction: 1–2 days post‑injection count array‑positive F1 progeny to decide whether the injection batch needs to be repeated.

steps.title: Apply hygromycin selection (day 3)
steps.instruction: Three days post‑injection, provided a hygR‑resistant plasmid was co‑injected, spread 500 µL of 5 mg/mL hygromycin B onto each plate, let the plates dry on the benchtop for ~30 minutes (or less), then return them to the 25 °C incubator.

steps.title: Screen dark marker‑positive worms (day 6)
steps.instruction: On day 6 post‑injection identify healthy adult worms that are non‑tdTomato but positive for the co‑injection marker. Transfer each candidate worm to an individual small NGM/OP50 plate and culture at 25 °C. Without hygromycin selection, perform worm chunking at the F1 generation if needed. Exclude worms with dim tdTomato expression; select only completely dark worms. Successful integrations typically yield 10–40 dark candidates; few dark worms indicate a poor injection.

steps.title: Identify uniform marker plates (day 9)
steps.instruction: On day 9 post‑injection examine plates for 100 % co‑injection marker expression in the progeny. These plates are potential integrants. Discard any plate that produces Unc worms (indicative of aneuploidy or non‑integrated animals).

steps.title: Validate candidate integrants
steps.instruction: Lines with uniform marker expression are candidate integrated lines. Confirm expression of the gene of interest by fluorescence microscopy or another appropriate assay. If fluorescence is not detectable, perform PCR genotyping.

steps.title: Consider lineage independence
steps.instruction: Integrated lines derived from the same P0 plate are not independent because individual lineages cannot be traced. To obtain distinct integrated lines, separate injected P0 worms onto individual plates or use several small pools of P0 animals after injection. Track progeny when possible; otherwise record only one integrated line per plate.
